concept: Bulk offset game manufacturing and sourcing

claims.text: PrintNinja’s game proofing guide warns that digitally printed proof components are not color accurate; custom card sizes or rounded corners require tooling priced by the account manager. Its proof turnaround is approximately 3-4 weeks and may increase for specialty options. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

PrintNinja’s physical-proof page lists an approximate 3–4-week turnaround and warns that digitally printed proof components are not color accurate. Custom card sizes and rounded corners require a tooling fee whose price is unspecified. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28)

Panda says it discards printing plates after every print run because storage is impractical; a reorder should not be budgeted on assumed plate reuse. This statement does not disclose reorder setup charges. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Delano requires a 50% production deposit and the balance before shipment. Its quoted material costs may change; labor pricing is firm for 30 days after quotation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja’s terms consider an order complete when the defect rate is under 2%; above 2% they allow a proportional refund or replacement copies at the supplier’s choice. This is a contractual remedy threshold, not a measured production defect rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja’s listed standard $450 physical proof covers one offset press sheet on 300 gsm coreless stock and a digitally printed tuck box; it excludes laminations, specialty options, instructions and rigid boxes. It cannot verify every selected production option. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)

Operator Brandon Rollins defines landed cost as manufacturing plus warehouse freight, customs and tariffs; Panda separately excludes shipping from manufacturing price. Compare delivered costs rather than only factory unit prices. (medium confidence)

Brandon Rollins advises evaluating sample ink and material quality and the supplier’s communication before selecting a printer; this is operator advice rather than comparative supplier test data. (low confidence)

PrintNinja says ocean delivery dates are approximate because customs, weather and holidays can disrupt shipping. Panda separately excludes door-to-door shipping from manufacturing prices; compare delivered project quotes rather than manufacturing-only unit prices. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Published general minimums differ: PrintNinja states 500 card games, Panda 1,500 games, and Delano 2,000 card or board games. These statements do not establish a reduced repeat-run minimum. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Panda describes digital proof approval, a near-final Pre-Production Copy before mass production, and a Mass Production Copy checkpoint before final assembly. These are manufacturer-described controls, not independent quality measurements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Panda excludes door-to-door shipping from manufacturing price and permits the buyer’s shipping agent to collect completed games without an additional pickup fee. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Delano advises 2-3 weeks for proofing followed by 6-8 weeks of off-season production, conditional on material availability; its September-to-early-December peak season can take longer. This is a production estimate, not delivered lead time. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja’s November 2, 2026 USD example for a 54-card poker deck in a printed tuck box lists Blue Core 280 gsm at $2.69 per deck ($1,343 total) for 500 decks and $1.94 ($1,943 total) for 1,000. Listed examples exclude shipping, sales tax and duties; they are not a quote for a different card count or packaging. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)

PrintNinja’s help page gives different shipping estimates: its card-specific answer says 3-4 weeks to print plus 6-8 weeks shipping, or about 2 weeks expedited; its general shipping answer says five weeks ocean or one week expedited. These are attributed estimates requiring project-specific reconciliation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja’s terms do not guarantee delivery dates and do not guarantee color accuracy without spot or Pantone color, even with hard-copy proofs. A proof approval therefore does not establish an exact CMYK color match across runs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja’s terms keep written quotes valid for 90 calendar days only for identical specifications and the named project/customer; changed specifications invalidate the original quotation. Reorder cost continuity therefore needs a fresh valid quote. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Panda describes a pre-production copy for approval before mass production, followed by a mass-production copy reviewed before final assembly. Door-to-door freight is excluded from its manufacturing price. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja’s November 2, 2026 USD table lists a 54-card poker deck in a printed tuck box, Blue Core 280 gsm, at $2.69 per deck and $1,343 total for 500 decks; the displayed unit price is rounded. Printing, packaging and electronic proofs are included; shipping, sales tax and duties are excluded. This example does not quote the commissioned game. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)
Delano says it reuses dies where possible; it does not promise indefinite die retention or a specific reorder saving in that statement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Looney Labs reports combining its same-format titles into shared reprint runs as low as 1000 copies. This is the publisher’s own production arrangement, not a universally available LongPack MOQ. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja warns that four-color offset color can vary within a run and more between runs. Looney Labs independently reports that cards made to its established size and corner-radius standards can still differ slightly. Identical digital artwork therefore does not establish indistinguishable physical reprints. (medium confidence)

PrintNinja’s help page gives different shipping estimates: the card-specific answer says 6–8 weeks after 3–4 weeks of printing; the general shipping answer says five weeks for ocean transit. Treat these as differing published estimates requiring project-specific confirmation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
